chunks: And by this chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on blood money for death caused by a well, beast, or mine in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'Jubarr' (liability without compensation) for specific natural hazards like wells, beasts of prey, and mines, distinguishing them from man-made structures requiring diya. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the concept of inherent danger (gharar) where the owner is exempt from blood money if the death results from the entity's natural state rather than negligence, reflecting a nuanced approach to accidental liability in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, 
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
(Being killed by) the well is ‘Jubarru’, (no wergild for it), and (being killed by) the beasts, is ‘Jubarru’ (no wergild for it), and (being killed by) the mines, is ‘Jubarru’ (no wergild for it’.
